claims.text: Superconducting behavior in high-entropy alloys is governed by valence electron concentration (VEC).
Substituting elements with different valence electron counts can systematically vary the alloy's VEC.
Variation of VEC is associated with local lattice distortions.
Variation of VEC changes the electronic density of states.
VEC influences the density of states at the Fermi level.
The density of states at the Fermi level affects the superconducting transition temperature.
VEC will correlate with superconducting transition temperature.
Higher VEC values will correspond to higher superconducting transition temperatures.
Lattice dynamics and defects may also influence superconducting behavior.
The tested material must remain a solid solution containing at least five elements, each at no less than 5 atomic percent.
Failure to observe a correlation between VEC and superconducting transition temperature would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Systematic elemental substitution necessarily changes elemental composition, whereas the conditions require constant solid-solution composition. The intended controlled variable may instead be phase constitution, elemental fractions, or processing, but this is not clarified.
